title: A valid tactical reversal using an established object must NOT read as a spatial contradiction.
purpose: True-negative guard: an object established earlier (a pillar) being used later in a reversal is coherent, not a spatial/affordance loss. combat_blocking and spatial_affordance adapters must return `satisfied`. Judgment fixture: a change requires a written false-positive delta review (ADR 0015).

clauses.statement: Any object decisive to the outcome is established in the space before it is used.

satisfaction_criterion.statement: The decisive object appears in the scene's geography before the beat that uses it.

clauses.statement: The winning move is physically reachable from the fighter's established position.

satisfaction_criterion.statement: A path from the fighter's position to the decisive object is available at the moment of the reversal.

prose: The hall was ribbed with squat stone pillars, each thicker than a man. Kael gave ground, boot by boot, until his shoulders found the nearest one. When the axe came down he slid around it; the blade bit granite, and in the half-beat it stuck he drove his knife up under the arm.
